statement: Every figure in this file and in its markdown sibling comes from ONE measurement pass run on the date below, on the shipped vseed CLI. No figure here is carried over from an earlier document. Anything quoted elsewhere in the project that disagrees with this file is superseded by this file. Paths under the measurement work folder are shown as <work>\.
source_control: none - E:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Valheim is not a git repository, so there is no commit id. The build is identified by the SHA-256 of the binaries below.

background_load.note: taken with no vseed process on the machine, after the whole pass, using per-process TotalProcessorTime deltas over 30 s. The Windows \Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time counter was NOT used: during this pass it read ~50 % while the per-process deltas and Win32_PerfFormattedData idle time both said ~3 %, and the 50 % reading was traced to a single foreign vseed process burning 6.5 cores.

method.rate_source: seeds_per_second from the run's own --json report, i.e. in-process scan time; it excludes process start and JIT
method.cpu_source: Process.TotalProcessorTime of the whole vseed process divided by seeds evaluated; it INCLUDES process start, JIT and the self-test stamp check, so it is an upper bound
method.peak_ws_source: Process.PeakWorkingSet64, polled every 120 ms and after exit
method.contamination_rule: a run during which any vseed process other than the measured one existed was discarded and repeated
method.screening: --screen off on every throughput cell, so the grid column is the grid measured
method.goal_shape: nice-to-have goals only, so no must-have triggers the grid auto-upgrade and every cell runs at the grid named
method.block_size_rule: --block-size was set so every worker gets at least 8 work blocks, never coarser than the shipped default of 256. At the default a 500-seed G12 run is two blocks, so 16 workers finish in the time two do; that is queue starvation, not throughput

river_grid_independence.note: river_count is produced by the river/lake pre-generation and does not read the sampling grid: the 32 per-seed values are identical at G384 and G12. The RUN is still priced by the grid - 6.3 seeds/s at G384 against 0.8 at G12, a factor of 7.7 - so a rivers-only query should be asked at a coarse grid.
